intro: AI agent systems engineer and technical founder. I have spent the past year on agentic systems and harness engineering, starting while I was finishing high school, where I was also wrestling team captain for two years. For most of that stretch I worked 13 to 14 hours a day on it, around school, my job and wrestling. I work across several harnesses instead of just one: OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness, Claude Desktop and Duet, Gemini Antigravity, Freebuff, ChatGPT Codex and Claude Code. I pick whichever has usage left and fits the job. Right now most of the work runs through Muse, Claude Duet and the DSH Fleet I am finishing. Three systems make up most of it. Ergon's employee agents are built to set themselves up — to watch how someone works, ask targeted questions, learn the role and keep a memory of the person, adding skills and tools as it goes. That loop is built and verified against simulated companies; the live model connection is the remaining piece before a first install. The DSH Fleet is a distributed orchestration layer: it runs dynamic swarms across desktop, virtual machine and browser surfaces, takes its tickets through Slack, and improves its own workflows, skills and plugin behaviour through a governed, checker-gated improvement programme run in rounds. OpenBell is my trading system: the desk runs a slot system — one slot per 15-minute market, every order placed by hand — and the research programme behind it is weight-space: I set the weights of tiny models directly, freeze their predictions before scoring, and score them in time order with costs counted. 1,200+ GitHub contributions in the last year. 4,000+ automated tests across five shipped systems.
